G9800.definition:
1.  any inarticulate sound, a sound, noise  , (Homer), etc.; of musical instruments, ψ. λωτοῦ, κιθάρας (Euripides) 
2.  a mere sound, empty sound, noise  , (Sophocles Tragicus); ψόφου πλέως, of Aeschylus, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9802.definition: a wine-cooler  , a vessel holding from 2 to 6 μετρηταί, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9804.definition: a morsel, bit  , ψωμοὶ ἀνδρόμεοι  gobbets   of man's flesh, Virgil's  sanies ac frusta  , (Odyssey by Homer); also in (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9805.definition: the itch, scurvy, scab, mange  , Lat.  scabies , impetigo, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9809.definition:
1.  to thrust, push, shove, force onwards   or  away  , λᾶαν ἄνω ὤθεσκε  he kept pushing   it upwards, (Odyssey by Homer); ἀπ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν νέφος ὦσεν Ἀθήνη (Iliad by Homer); ἐκ μηροῦ δόρυ ὦσε  he forced   the spear from the thigh, (Iliad by Homer); ὦσαί τινα ἀφ᾽ ἵππων (Iliad by Homer); ὦσαι ἑαυτὸν ἐς τὸ πῦρ  to rush   into the fire, (Herdotus Historicus); so, ὠθ. τινὰ ἐπὶ κεφαλήν  to throw   him headlong down, (Plato Philosophus); κατὰ πετρῶν (Euripides); ὦσαι τὴν θύραν  to force   the door, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  to push   or  force back   in battle, (Iliad by Homer) 
3.  to thrust out, banish  , [  variant  dates Tragica Adespota  ; ὦσαί τινα φυγάδα (Plato Philosophus); ὠθ. τινα ἄθαπτον (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4.  metaphorically , ὠθ. τὰ πρήγματα  to push   matters  on, hurry   them, (Herdotus Historicus) 
5.  absolute , ὦσα παρέξ  pushed off   from land, (Odyssey by Homer); ὤθει βιαίως (Euripides) 
6. Mid., mostly in aor1,  to thrust   or  push from oneself, push   or  force back, repulse  , especially in battle, τείχεος ἂψ ὤσασθαι (Iliad by Homer); ὤσασθαι προτὶ Ἴλιον, προτὶ ἄστυ (Iliad by Homer); ὤσασθαι τὴν ἵππον (Herdotus Historicus); ὠσαμένων τὸ κέρας (Thucydides) 
7. Pass.  to be thrust on, to fall violently  , ἐπὶ κεφαλήν (Herdotus Historicus); πρὸς βίαν (Euripides) 
8.  to force one's way  , (Xenophon Historicus):  to crowd on, throng  , like ὠστίζομαι, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9814.definition:
1.  ripeness of fruits  , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2.  the bloom of youth  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9820.definition:
1.  a useful   or  serviceable thing, a service, benefit  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. generally,  use, advantage, profit  , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9823.definition:
1.  flexible, pliant  : στρεπτὸς χιτών a shirt  of chain-armour  , Lat.  lorica annulata , (Iliad by Homer); στρεπταὶ λύγοι  pliant   withs, (Euripides):  twined, wreathed  , [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   
2. στρεπτός, οῦ,  a collar of twisted   or  linked metal  , Lat.  torques , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
3. of pastry,  a twist   or  roll  , (Demosthenes Orator) 
4.  metaphorically   to be bent   or  turned  , στρεπτοὶ καὶ θεοὶ αὐτοί the gods themselves  may be turned   (by prayer), (Iliad by Homer); στρ. γλῶσσα  a glib, pliant   tongue, (Iliad by Homer) 
5.  bent, curved  , of a pick-axe, (Euripides); of a bow, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9839.definition:
1.  the twentieth  , (Odyssey by Homer); epic also ἐεικοστός, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. εἰκοστή, ἡ,  a tax of a twentieth  , Lat.  vicesima , levied by the Athenians on imports and exports from the allies in lieu of tribute, (Thucydides) (ML)

G9843.definition: without exception ( εν ακί at is  1Kgs.15.22  a transliterration of אֵ֣ין נָקִ֔י)
